### Start Caddy with example config

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/crates/remote/README.md

Runs Caddy using the provided Caddyfile.example. The first run installs a local CA certificate and may prompt for your password.

```bash
caddy run --config Caddyfile.example
```

### Setup Script Examples

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/settings/projects-repositories.mdx

Commands to prepare the development environment before the coding agent starts. Setup scripts run in the repository's root directory and execute once when the workspace starts, not on every agent message.

```bash
# Node.js project
npm install
```

```bash
# Python project
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

```bash
# Multiple commands
npm install && npm run build:deps
```

```bash
# Rust project
cargo fetch
```

### Start all services with Docker Compose from crates/remote

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/local-development.mdx

Run from the `crates/remote` directory to start PostgreSQL, ElectricSQL, Remote Server, and Relay Server. The remote server binds to `127.0.0.1:3000` only and is not accessible from other machines; use a reverse proxy for production.

```bash
cd crates/remote
docker compose --env-file .env.remote -f docker-compose.yml up --build
```

### Start colima Docker VM for cross builds

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/RELEASING.md

One-time setup for local releases. Give the VM at most half the Mac's RAM to avoid swapping and freezing; build refuses a VM bigger than half the RAM and runs about one rustc job per 2 GB of VM memory. Stop with `colima stop` and quit Docker Desktop while building.

```bash
colima start --cpu 4 --memory 6 --disk 100
```

### Connect desktop client to local server

```bash

pnpm install
pnpm run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Docker Mode: Run Docker stack and Caddy

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/mobile-testing.md

Two-terminal setup for Docker mode. Terminal 1 starts the Docker stack with Tailscale URLs; Terminal 2 runs Caddy. First run rebuilds the frontend with the URLs baked in, which takes a few minutes; subsequent runs are cached.

```bash
# Terminal 1 — Docker stack
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 \
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 \
pnpm remote:dev
```

```bash
# Terminal 2 — Caddy
caddy run --config Caddyfile
```

--------------------------------

### Docker mode setup (2 terminals)

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/mobile-testing.md

Run the app in Docker mode using two terminals. Terminal 1 starts the remote dev server with environment variables, Terminal 2 runs Caddy. Then echo the phone URL to access the app.

```bash
# Terminal 1
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 \
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 \
pnpm remote:dev

# Terminal 2
caddy run --config Caddyfile

# On phone
echo "https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001"
```

### start_workspace Tool Parameters JSON

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

Example JSON parameters for the start_workspace tool. Creates a new workspace, links it to the issue, generates a feature branch, and starts the coding agent in an isolated environment.

```json
{
  "name": "User registration with email validation",
  "executor": "claude-code",
  "repositories": [
    {
      "repo_id": "987fcdeb-51a2-3d4e-b678-426614174001",
      "branch": "main"
    }
  ],
  "issue_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

### Handle errors gracefully with `|| true`

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/settings/projects-repositories.mdx

### Install Docker (Ubuntu/Debian)

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Installs Docker and adds the current user to the docker group. Log out and back in for group changes to take effect.

```bash
# Install Docker (Ubuntu/Debian)
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# Log out and back in for group changes to take effect
```

### Stop and remove all data with docker compose down -v

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/local-development.mdx

Stops all services and removes volumes for a fresh start.

```bash
docker compose down -v
```

--------------------------------

### start_workspace

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

Creates a workspace and starts its first coding-agent session. Requires name, executor, and repositories. Optional parameters include prompt, variant, and issue_id.

```APIDOC
## start_workspace

### Description
Creates a workspace and starts its first coding-agent session.

### Parameters
#### Required Parameters
- **name** - Required - Workspace name
- **executor** - Required - Executor type (case-insensitive, accepts hyphens or underscores)
- **repositories** - Required - Array of objects with `repo_id` (UUID) and `branch`

#### Optional Parameters
- **prompt** - Optional - Workspace prompt; if omitted, linked issue's title and description are used
- **variant** - Optional - Variant
- **issue_id** - Optional - If provided, workspace is automatically linked to the remote issue

### Returns
Workspace ID
```

--------------------------------

### Dev mode setup (4 terminals)

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/mobile-testing.md

Run the app in dev mode using four terminals: Docker backends, Vite dev server, Caddy, and optionally the desktop client. Then echo the phone URL to access the app.

```bash
# Terminal 1 — Docker backends
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 \
pnpm remote:dev

# Terminal 2 — Vite
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 \
pnpm --filter @vibe/remote-web dev

# Terminal 3 — Caddy
caddy run --config Caddyfile.dev

# Terminal 4 (optional) — Desktop client
VK_SHARED_API_BASE=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 \
VK_SHARED_RELAY_API_BASE=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 \
pnpm run dev

# On phone
echo "https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001"
```

### Restart Electric service with env file

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/local-development.mdx

Restarts the Electric service using the .env.remote environment file, useful when ElectricSQL fails to connect.

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env.remote -f docker-compose.yml restart electric
```

--------------------------------

### Deploy with Docker Compose

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Build and start all services using the production compose file with the remote environment file. The first build takes 10-15 minutes; subsequent builds are faster due to Docker caching. Use the second command to view logs.

```bash
cd crates/remote

# Build and start all services
docker compose --env-file ../../.env.remote -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build

# View logs
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f
```

--------------------------------

### Troubleshoot database connection refused

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Check database logs and restart the server if it started before the database was ready.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs remote-db
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml restart remote-server
```

```javascript
const apiConfig = {

  }
};
```

--------------------------------

### Combining Multiple Cleanup Commands

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/settings/projects-repositories.mdx

Examples of chaining cleanup commands with && and using || true to ignore failures. Cleanup scripts should be idempotent—use || true to prevent failures when there's nothing to clean up.

```bash
# Chain commands with &&
docker compose down && rm -rf tmp/
```

```bash
# Format code after agent changes
npx prettier --write . && npx eslint --fix .
```

```bash
# Rust formatting and linting
cargo fmt && cargo clippy --fix --allow-dirty
```

```bash
# Use || true to ignore failures
pkill -f "node server.js" || true
rm -rf .cache/ || true
```

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

```APIDOC
## get_issue

### Description
Get detailed issue information.

### Parameters
#### Required Parameters
- **issue_id** - Required - The ID of the issue.

### Response
Returns full issue details with tags, relationships, sub-issues, and PRs.
```

--------------------------------

### Dry run: build and smoke test locally

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/RELEASING.md

Optional step to verify the release locally without publishing. Builds all 6 platforms (first run also builds the Docker image) and then installs the packed CLI and runs it against the built assets. On a HEAD without a v* tag, builds are named v<version>-dryrun into release-out/ and publish refuses them.

```bash
scripts/release-local.sh build    # all 6 platforms; the first run also builds the Docker image
```

```bash
scripts/release-local.sh smoke    # installs the packed CLI and runs it against the built assets
```

### Test relay tunnel end-to-end

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/crates/remote/README.md

```bash
export VK_SHARED_API_BASE=https://localhost:3001
export VK_SHARED_RELAY_API_BASE=https://relay.localhost:3001

pnpm run dev
```

```bash
export VK_SHARED_API_BASE=https://localhost:3001
export VK_SHARED_RELAY_API_BASE=https://relay.localhost:3001
export VK_TUNNEL=1
```

### Example: rebase onto main excluding develop commits

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/core-features/resolving-rebase-conflicts.mdx

Example scenario showing how to rebase only your commits onto main after accidentally basing your task on develop. Replace the commit hash with the last commit before your work.

```bash
# Find the last commit before your work started (e.g., in the git log)
# Then rebase only your commits onto main
git rebase 64d504c94d076070d17affd3f84be63b34515445 --onto main
```

### Create .env.remote Configuration File

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/local-development.mdx

Create this file in crates/remote/ with the required JWT secret and optional settings. Configure at least one OAuth provider. For production, add PUBLIC_BASE_URL and REMOTE_SERVER_PORTS. Never commit this file to version control.

```env
# Required - JWT secret for authentication
VIBEKANBAN_REMOTE_JWT_SECRET=<paste_your_generated_secret_here>

# Optional - Password for ElectricSQL database role (electric_sync user)
ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD=

# OAuth — configure at least one provider. Leave the other empty or remove it.
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=your_github_client_id
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=your_github_client_secret

# Google OAuth (leave empty if not using Google login)
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Relay (required for relay/tunnel features)
# For plain HTTP local dev:
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8082

# Email invitations (optional — leave empty to disable)
LOOPS_EMAIL_API_KEY=

# Loops transactional email template IDs (optional — defaults are the upstream templates).
# Override these with your own Loops account template IDs if using a custom Loops account.
LOOPS_INVITE_TEMPLATE_ID=cmhvy2wgs3s13z70i1pxakij9
LOOPS_REVIEW_READY_TEMPLATE_ID=cmj47k5ge16990iylued9by17
LOOPS_REVIEW_FAILED_TEMPLATE_ID=cmj49ougk1c8s0iznavijdqpo
```

```bash
mint dev
```

### Cleanup Script Command Examples

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/settings/projects-repositories.mdx

Commands to clean up resources and stop background processes when a workspace closes. Cleanup scripts should be idempotent—safe to run even if resources don't exist.

```bash
docker compose down
```

```bash
pkill -f "node server.js"
```

```bash
rm -rf dist/ .cache/
```

```bash
pg_ctl stop -D /usr/local/var/postgres
```

```bash
lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9 2>/dev/null
```

### Generate JWT secret with openssl

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/crates/remote/README.md

Generates a random base64-encoded 48-byte secret for the VIBEKANBAN_REMOTE_JWT_SECRET environment variable.

```bash
openssl rand -base64 48
```

### Create .env.remote configuration file

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/crates/remote/README.md

Required environment configuration for the remote service. Includes JWT secret, database password, auth options (GitHub/Google OAuth or self-host local auth), and optional settings like Loops email template IDs.

```env
# Required
VIBEKANBAN_REMOTE_JWT_SECRET=replace_with_openssl_rand_base64_48
ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD=replace_with_secure_password

# Configure at least one auth option
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Or use bootstrap local auth for self-hosting
SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_EMAIL=
SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_PASSWORD=

# Optional
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8082
VITE_PUBLIC_REACT_VIRTUOSO_LICENSE_KEY=
LOOPS_EMAIL_API_KEY=

# Loops transactional email template IDs (optional — defaults are the upstream templates).
# Override these with your own Loops account template IDs if using a custom Loops account.
LOOPS_INVITE_TEMPLATE_ID=cmhvy2wgs3s13z70i1pxakij9
LOOPS_REVIEW_READY_TEMPLATE_ID=cmj47k5ge16990iylued9by17
LOOPS_REVIEW_FAILED_TEMPLATE_ID=cmj49ougk1c8s0iznavijdqpo
```

--------------------------------

### Dev Mode: Run four terminals

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/mobile-testing.md

Four-terminal setup for Dev Mode with Vite hot reload. Terminal 1 runs Docker backends without frontend build; Terminal 2 runs Vite dev server; Terminal 3 runs Caddy with Caddyfile.dev; Terminal 4 (optional) runs local desktop client. Vite binds to localhost:3002, and Caddyfile.dev uses localhost to avoid IPv6/IPv4 mismatch on macOS.

```bash
# Terminal 1 — Docker backends (no frontend build needed)
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 \
pnpm remote:dev
```

```bash
# Terminal 2 — Vite dev server (hot reload)
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 \
pnpm --filter @vibe/remote-web dev
```

```bash
# Terminal 3 — Caddy (dev config)
caddy run --config Caddyfile.dev
```

```bash
# Terminal 4 (optional) — Local desktop client
VK_SHARED_API_BASE=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 \
VK_SHARED_RELAY_API_BASE=https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 \
pnpm run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Code group with multiple languages: JavaScript, Python, cURL

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md

Example of a code group in Mintlify showing the same API request in three languages: JavaScript (Node.js), Python, and cURL. Each uses an Authorisation header with a Bearer token.

```javascript
const response = await fetch('/api/endpoint', {
  headers: { Authorisation: `Bearer ${apiKey}` }
});
```

```python
import requests
response = requests.get('/api/endpoint',
  headers={'Authorisation': f'Bearer {api_key}'})
```

```curl
curl -X GET '/api/endpoint' \
  -H 'Authorisation: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY'
```

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

```env
SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_PASSWORD=replace_with_a_strong_password
```

### Quick health checks

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/crates/remote/README.md

Checks the health endpoints of the remote API and relay API. If the relay health endpoint returns HTML instead of {"status":"ok"}, Caddy host routing is incorrect.

```bash
curl -sk https://localhost:3001/v1/health
curl -sk https://relay.localhost:3001/health
```

### Reset Docker build cache

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/RELEASING.md

Clears Cargo's Docker volumes used for cross builds. Use when a VM crash leaves broken files, e.g., 'failed to unpack package ... invalid gzip header'. Empty downloads are dropped automatically at build start; this handles other corruption.

```bash
scripts/release-local.sh reset-cache
```

### Add Web Companion to Create React App

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/core-features/testing-your-application.mdx

Add the companion to your src/index.js or src/index.tsx for Create React App projects.

```jsx
import { VibeKanbanWebCompanion } from 'vibe-kanban-web-companion';
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';

const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root'));
root.render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <VibeKanbanWebCompanion />
    <App />
  </React.StrictMode>
);
```

### Add Web Companion to Vite

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/core-features/testing-your-application.mdx

Add the companion to your src/main.jsx or src/main.tsx for Vite projects.

```jsx
import { VibeKanbanWebCompanion } from "vibe-kanban-web-companion";
import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import App from "./App";

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(

  </React.StrictMode>
);
```

### Add Web Companion to Next.js

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/core-features/testing-your-application.mdx

Add the companion to your pages/_app.js or pages/_app.tsx for Next.js projects.

```jsx
import { VibeKanbanWebCompanion } from 'vibe-kanban-web-companion'
import type { AppProps } from 'next/app'

function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }: AppProps) {
  return (
    <>
      <VibeKanbanWebCompanion />
      <Component {...pageProps} />
    </>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### buildExpectedServerProof() - expected server proof HMAC

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/scripts/relay-test-client/index.html

Builds the expected server proof by HMAC-SHA256 over the concatenation of SERVER_PROOF_CONTEXT, enrollment ID, browser public key, and server public key bytes, using the confirmation key.

```javascript
async function buildExpectedServerProof(sharedKey, enrollmentId, browserPkBytes, serverPkBytes) { const confirmationKey = await deriveConfirmationKey(sharedKey); const proofInput = concatBytes( SERVER_PROOF_CONTEXT, parseUuidBytes(enrollmentId), browserPkBytes, serverPkBytes, ); return hmacSha256(confirmationKey, proofInput); }
```

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/RELEASING.md

Bumps the version, commits the bump, creates a local tag v<version>.<timestamp>, then builds and runs the smoke test. The tag stays local until publish.

```bash
./bump-version.sh                 # commits the bump and creates tag v<version>.<timestamp>
```

```bash
scripts/release-local.sh build
```


### Add swap space for out-of-memory errors

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Create and enable a 2GB swap file to mitigate build failures due to insufficient RAM.

```bash
sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile
```

### Publish release

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/RELEASING.md

Runs the release publish script. It pushes the tag, creates a GitHub pre-release with assets, runs the smoke test against the real release, and publishes to npm under next. It asks before each stage; answering no at the npm question stops there.

```bash
scripts/release-local.sh publish
```

--------------------------------

### buildClientProof() - client proof HMAC

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/scripts/relay-test-client/index.html

Builds the client proof by HMAC-SHA256 over the concatenation of CLIENT_PROOF_CONTEXT, enrollment ID bytes, and browser public key bytes, using the confirmation key.

```javascript
async function buildClientProof(sharedKey, enrollmentId, browserPkBytes) { const confirmationKey = await deriveConfirmationKey(sharedKey); const proofInput = concatBytes( CLIENT_PROOF_CONTEXT, parseUuidBytes(enrollmentId), browserPkBytes, ); return hmacSha256(confirmationKey, proofInput); }
```

--------------------------------

### Create Caddyfile with reverse proxy config

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/mobile-testing.md

Creates a Caddyfile that proxies https://$TS_HOSTNAME:3001 to localhost:3000 and https://$TS_HOSTNAME:8443 to localhost:8082, using the generated certificates. Separate ports avoid conflicts.

```bash
cat > Caddyfile << EOF
${TS_HOSTNAME}:3001 {
    tls ${TS_HOSTNAME}.crt ${TS_HOSTNAME}.key
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

${TS_HOSTNAME}:8443 {
    tls ${TS_HOSTNAME}.crt ${TS_HOSTNAME}.key
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8082
}
EOF
```

--------------------------------

### Backup database with pg_dump

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Create a SQL dump of the remote database into a timestamped file. Run from the crates/remote directory.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec remote-db \
  pg_dump -U remote remote > backup_$(date +%Y%m%d).sql
```

### Complete Workflow Steps Prompt

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

Multi-step workflow prompt covering organisation, project, issue, and workspace operations. Each step uses the appropriate MCP tool (list_organizations, list_projects, list_issues, create_issue, assign_issue, start_workspace) to manage the full planning-to-execution flow.

```text
1. List organisations to find the organisation ID
2. List projects in the organisation to find the project ID
3. List issues in the project filtered by status
4. Create a new issue for "Add user profile page"
5. Assign a team member to the issue
6. Start a workspace session for the issue using Amp on the develop branch
```

### Planning and Issue Creation Prompt

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

Describe a feature and append 'then turn this plan into issues' to have the MCP client use the create_issue tool to break it into individual issues and add them to the Vibe Kanban project.

```text
I need to build a user authentication system with the following features:
- User registration with email validation
- Login/logout functionality
- Password reset capability
- Session management
- Protected routes

Then turn this plan into issues.
```

--------------------------------

### Create docker-compose.prod.yml

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Create this file in the crates/remote directory. It defines services for Caddy, PostgreSQL, Electric, and the remote server, with health checks and volume definitions.

```yaml
services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      DOMAIN: ${DOMAIN}
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    depends_on:
      - remote-server

  remote-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "wal_level=logical"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: remote
      POSTGRES_USER: remote
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-remote}
    volumes:
      - remote-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U remote -d remote"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 5s

  electric:
    image: electricsql/electric:1.4.13
    working_dir: /app
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://electric_sync:${ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD}@remote-db:5432/remote?sslmode=disable
      PG_PROXY_PORT: 65432
      LOGICAL_PUBLISHER_HOST: electric
      AUTH_MODE: insecure
      ELECTRIC_INSECURE: true
      ELECTRIC_MANUAL_TABLE_PUBLISHING: true
      ELECTRIC_USAGE_REPORTING: false
      ELECTRIC_FEATURE_FLAGS: allow_subqueries,tagged_subqueries
    volumes:
      - electric-data:/app/persistent
    depends_on:
      remote-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      remote-server:
        condition: service_healthy

  remote-server:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: crates/remote/Dockerfile
      args:
        VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL: ${VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL:-}
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      remote-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      RUST_LOG: info,remote=info
      SERVER_DATABASE_URL: postgres://remote:${DB_PASSWORD:-remote}@remote-db:5432/remote
      SERVER_LISTEN_ADDR: 0.0.0.0:8081
      ELECTRIC_URL: http://electric:3000
      SERVER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL: https://${DOMAIN}
      GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID:-}
      GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET:-}
      GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID:-}
      GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET:-}
      VIBEKANBAN_REMOTE_JWT_SECRET: ${VIBEKANBAN_REMOTE_JWT_SECRET}
      ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD: ${ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD}
      LOOPS_EMAIL_API_KEY: ${LOOPS_EMAIL_API_KEY:-}
      LOOPS_INVITE_TEMPLATE_ID: ${LOOPS_INVITE_TEMPLATE_ID:-cmhvy2wgs3s13z70i1pxakij9}
      LOOPS_REVIEW_READY_TEMPLATE_ID: ${LOOPS_REVIEW_READY_TEMPLATE_ID:-cmj47k5ge16990iylued9by17}
      LOOPS_REVIEW_FAILED_TEMPLATE_ID: ${LOOPS_REVIEW_FAILED_TEMPLATE_ID:-cmj49ougk1c8s0iznavijdqpo}
      SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_EMAIL: ${SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_EMAIL:-}
      SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_PASSWORD: ${SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_PASSWORD:-}
      AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME:
      AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY:
      AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME:
      AZURE_STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL:
      AZURE_STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_URL:
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--spider", "-q", "http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 10s

volumes:
  remote-db-data:
  electric-data:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:
```

--------------------------------

### Manual MCP Server Configuration for Vibe Kanban

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

Add this JSON to your coding agent's MCP servers configuration to connect to Vibe Kanban's local MCP server. The `--mcp` flag launches the local MCP stdio server; any additional arguments after it are passed through to the `vibe-kanban-mcp` binary.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vibe_kanban": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "vibe-kanban@latest", "--mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Run remote crate tests with cargo test

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/crates/remote/AGENTS.md

Runs the test suite for the remote crate. SQLx compile-time checks require either a running Postgres or offline query data in the `.sqlx/` directory; use `pnpm run remote:prepare-db` to set that up.

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path crates/remote/Cargo.toml
```

--------------------------------

### Add GitHub OAuth credentials to .env.remote

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/mobile-testing.md

Sets GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET in crates/remote/.env.remote. Replace with your own values. The file is gitignored; replace existing variables if present.

```bash
# Replace with your own values
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
```

--------------------------------

### Restore database with psql

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Restore a SQL dump into the remote database. Use the -T flag to disable pseudo-TTY allocation.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec -T remote-db \
  psql -U remote remote < backup_20240101.sql
```

--------------------------------

### Authenticate with Azure CLI

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/azure-repos-integration.mdx

Signs in to Azure via web browser prompts. Required for the integration to work.

```bash
az login
```

--------------------------------

### Create .env.remote environment file

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Create this file in the repository root with required secrets and optional configuration for authentication, email, and attachments.

```env
# Required secrets
VIBEKANBAN_REMOTE_JWT_SECRET=<your_generated_jwt_secret>
ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD=<secure_password_for_electric>
DB_PASSWORD=<secure_database_password>

# Your domain
DOMAIN=your-domain.com

# Relay API base URL (required if you enable relay/tunnel)
VITE_RELAY_API_BASE_URL=https://relay.your-domain.com

# Authentication — configure at least one provider, or set bootstrap local auth credentials.
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=your_github_client_id
GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=your_github_client_secret
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=
SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_EMAIL=
SELF_HOST_LOCAL_AUTH_PASSWORD=

# Email (optional — leave empty to disable invitation emails)
LOOPS_EMAIL_API_KEY=

# Loops transactional email template IDs (optional — defaults are the upstream templates).
# Override these with your own Loops account template IDs if using a custom Loops account.
LOOPS_INVITE_TEMPLATE_ID=cmhvy2wgs3s13z70i1pxakij9
LOOPS_REVIEW_READY_TEMPLATE_ID=cmj47k5ge16990iylued9by17
LOOPS_REVIEW_FAILED_TEMPLATE_ID=cmj49ougk1c8s0iznavijdqpo

# Attachments (optional — only set when you want issue attachments enabled)
AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME=
AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY=
AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME=issue-attachments
AZURE_STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL=
AZURE_STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_URL=
```

--------------------------------

### update_cleanup_script

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx

Updates a repository's cleanup script. Requires a repository ID and the new script content.

```APIDOC
## update_cleanup_script

### Description
Updates a repository's cleanup script.

### Parameters
#### Required Parameters
- **repo_id** - Required - The repository ID
- **script** - Required - The new cleanup script

### Returns
Update confirmation
```

--------------------------------

### Check disk usage on Linux

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/workspaces/managing-workspaces.mdx

Run in terminal to see the size of the workspace worktrees directory on Linux. Uses the default /var/tmp location.

```bash
du -sh /var/tmp/vibe-kanban/worktrees
```

--------------------------------

### Restart ElectricSQL service

Source: https://github.com/bloopai/vibe-kanban/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/deploy-docker.mdx

Restart the Electric service after ensuring the Remote Server is healthy and ELECTRIC_ROLE_PASSWORD matches.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml restart electric
```
